title: Rosalind and the Hollow
premise: Isandro Lockridge keeps the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in stolen memories, borrowed years, and other impossible things, hiding behind her role as a nameless clerk in a country that was officially erased from every map a generation ago. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, their returning power starts dissolving the borders that keep her country hidden—and with it, everyone who lives there. Hunted by a god-touched magistrate and betrayed by the guildmaster she serves, Isandro discovers that the ledger itself is a key: every memory she has ever recorded can open one door out of the Hollow. To save her people she must surrender her own past, memory by memory, until only the truth of what she stole remains—ending with her walking through the last door as a stranger, carrying her country's history into a world that will finally have to remember it.
about_author: Wren Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing the personal effects of displaced families before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about records, ruins, and the people history forgets to count.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She catalogs a night's takings—a widow's grief, a soldier's courage—revealing the guild's trade and her own careful invisibility. Emotional beat: quiet complicity; she tells herself bookkeeping is not stealing.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A client pays in memories of a prayer that was actually answered—the first in living memory. The guild dismisses it as counterfeit. Beat: unease; Isandro alone notices the memory's impossible texture.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She walks the Hollow's fog-bound streets, establishing the erased nation and its people who exist by mutual pretense. Beat: belonging tinged with claustrophobia; invisibility as both shelter and cage.

chapters.title: Magistrate Veyl Arrives
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. A god-touched magistrate crosses the border that should not admit him, hunting the source of answered prayers. Beat: cold menace; his faith makes him more dangerous than any soldier.

chapters.title: Inventory of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Guildmaster Corvane orders the vault sealed and all god-related memories destroyed. Isandro secretly copies one entry instead. Beat: first small rebellion; fear sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Widow Remembered
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She traces the answered prayer to a dying woman whose memories were never sold. The woman speaks a god's name and the room grows warmer. Beat: awe and dread entwined.

chapters.title: The Guild's First Law
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Flashback to how the guild helped erase the country, trading away its name to hide it from conquest. Beat: guilt rationalized; Corvane believes erasure was mercy.

chapters.title: Veyl Takes a Confession
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. He interrogates a memory-thief and literally reads the crime from the man's mind, leaving him hollowed. Beat: horror; establishes the price of being found.

chapters.title: Doors in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Studying the copied entry, she realizes each recorded memory resonates like a lock—and the ledger is a ring of keys. Beat: dawning hope; the bookkeeping was never neutral.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Stole Herself
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She examines her own earliest recorded memory and finds a gap: someone took her childhood. Beat: identity shaken; even the archivist has been archived.

chapters.title: Border Fires
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The Hollow's edges begin to smolder where prayers burn through the concealment. Panic spreads; the guild blames smugglers. Beat: the invisible country becoming visible, catastrophically.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Fog Market
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She seeks the smuggler Sefa, who once traded in borders themselves, and buys passage-knowledge with a stolen summer. Beat: wary alliance; paying with pieces of herself begins.

chapters.title: Corvane's Second Law
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He learns gods are returning because the guild's original bargain is expiring, and decides the answer is a larger erasure: the people's memories of ever having been a nation. Beat: chilling logic; corruption dressed as protection.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Unremembered
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the undercity she finds worshippers keeping the old gods alive in secret for generations. Beat: warmth and belonging; the first community that sees her.

chapters.title: Veyl Hears Singing
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. Drawn by the choir, he witnesses a genuine miracle and wavers—his god answers, but not as doctrine promised. Beat: crisis of faith; the hunter doubting the hunt.

chapters.title: Ledger Burned
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Corvane burns the public ledgers to destroy the 'keys.' Isandro realizes she holds the only complete copy—in her head, memorized over years. Beat: terror turning to resolve; the clerk becomes the archive.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She reveals the door out requires a memory freely given by every soul who wishes to leave—but Corvane plans to take them by force. Beat: stakes clarified; consent versus coercion as the story's moral axis.

chapters.title: The Gap in Her Childhood
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following the gap in her own memory, she finds the guild record of its purchase: her mother sold Isandro's childhood to buy the family's place in the Hollow. Beat: grief and fury; belonging bought at an unbearable price.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Vault
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She confronts Corvane; he offers her partnership and her missing memories back if she helps him erase the nation's identity. Beat: temptation; power offered exactly when she feels most powerless.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She refuses and flees with the choir's help, hunted now by both guild and magistrate. Beat: point of no return; choosing justice outside every law.

chapters.title: What Veyl Keeps
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. He captures Isandro but cannot bring himself to hollow her; instead he asks what she knows about his god. Beat: enemy softening; two truths colliding honestly.

chapters.title: The God of Doors
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In a ruined shrine, the old god of thresholds answers her—not with power but with a question: what will you carry through? Beat: revelation; the exit demands a witness, not a weapon.

chapters.title: Corvane's Great Erasure
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He begins mass-harvesting the population's national memory, storing it in a new master ledger. People wander their own streets as strangers. Beat: darkest turn; the country dissolving from within.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Harvest House
chapters.summary: Isandro and Sefa raid a harvest site, freeing memories back into their owners. Veyl, ordered to stop them, instead looks away. Beat: first victory; solidarity forged in action.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Choir
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A choir member, terrified for his children, sells her location to Corvane. Beat: heartbreak; betrayal born of love, not malice.

chapters.title: Captured
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Corvane takes her and begins extracting the memorized ledger, memory by memory. Each removal erases a piece of her. Beat: agony; the archive being unwritten.

chapters.title: Veyl's Choice
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. Watching Isandro emptied, he finally understands his god's silence: divinity lives in what people refuse to surrender. He turns on Corvane. Beat: redemption; the law breaking toward justice.

chapters.title: The Vault War
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Veyl, Sefa, and the choir assault the vault while Corvane channels the harvested nation-memory into himself, becoming something vast and hollow. Beat: chaos and sacrifice; the climax ignites.

chapters.title: What Corvane Became
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Drunk on a whole country's remembering, he experiences every grief at once and understands too late what mercy actually was. Beat: tragic collapse; power's corruption completing itself.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Nearly empty, she reaches the threshold-god's door. It will open only for what she still carries: one memory, freely kept. Beat: the choice; she keeps not her childhood but the moment she chose to refuse.

chapters.title: Opening the Way
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She gives the door her final held memory—the ledger itself—and it opens onto the world beyond the maps. Beat: transcendence through loss; the key was always the giving.

chapters.title: Exodus
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The people of the Hollow pass through, each leaving one freely given memory to hold the door wide. Sefa stays to guide stragglers. Beat: bittersweet procession; a nation walking out of erasure.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. Corvane, unraveling, tries to force the door and is refused—it opens only for gifts. He collapses into the fog that made them. Beat: justice without cruelty; the door itself judges.

chapters.title: On the Far Side
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The survivors wake in a living country that must now acknowledge them. Isandro remembers almost nothing of herself but knows exactly what she did. Beat: disorientation and peace; identity rebuilt from action rather than past.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Survivors bring her scraps of what they chose to keep, asking her to write them down so no one is erased again. Beat: healing purpose; the thief becomes a keeper of given things.

chapters.title: Veyl's Penance
chapters.summary: Veyl's POV. He surrenders his magistrate's authority to the refugees' council, asking to be judged by the people he hunted. Beat: accountability; justice outside the law applied to its enforcer.

chapters.title: What the Gods Wanted
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At a new shrine she finally asks the threshold-god why the prayers returned. Answer: gods come back wherever people refuse to be forgotten. Beat: thematic resolution; memory as sacred act.

chapters.title: A Name Returned
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The council restores the country's true name, recovered from a memory Sefa guarded for decades. Isandro learns her own birth-name for the first time since childhood. Beat: restoration; belonging reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Door Held Open
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She establishes an order of door-keepers who record memories freely given, ensuring the way home stays open for those still lost. Beat: legacy; the arc from invisible clerk to visible founder.

chapters.title: Rosalind
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, closing. Standing at the threshold at dawn, she signs the new ledger with her restored name—Rosalind Lockridge—and steps fully into the remembered world. Beat: quiet triumph; the hollow filled, the self made whole.
